title: Build explorable explanations
principle: When the goal is understanding, let readers manipulate the model—sliders, scrubbers, linked views—instead of only reading a static takeaway chart.
procedure: State the misconception or hard idea the explorable must correct.
Pick one interactive control that changes the underlying model (not cosmetic filters).
Link views so one action updates explanation + visual together.
Provide a default path for skim readers; depth for explorers.
Instrument failure: if interaction doesn’t change understanding, cut it.
examplePrompts:
Design an explorable for <concept>.

Misconception to correct: <…>
One primary control: <slider/scrubber/toggle>
Linked outputs: <chart + plain-language readout>
Static fallback summary for no-JS / reduced motion.
Do not decorate; the control must change the model.
tips: Amelia’s public work centers interactive essays and viz craft.
Explorables beat poster charts when the reader must build intuition.

workedExamples.title: Poster chart → explorable
workedExamples.before: One static bar chart + long caption.
workedExamples.after: Slider on the key parameter; chart + sentence update together.
workedExamples.body: Interaction teaches the model; caption alone often doesn’t.

workedExamples.title: Cosmetic filters
workedExamples.after: Control that changes the calculation readers must grasp.
workedExamples.body: If the model doesn’t move, it’s chrome—not an explorable.

antiPatterns: No static summary for accessibility / reduced motion.
